scope.frame: characters of the free group F_n in SL(2, C); the moves R_ij: a_i -> a_i a_j and L_ij: a_i -> a_j a_i
scope.object: the weave of n records for every n >= 2; every finite subgroup of SU(2) on the class reading
scope.hypotheses: the rank-two target SL(2, C) and the requirement of a non-trivial common character are inputs; higher-rank targets are open (P-209)

claim_one_line: THE COMMON POINT FOR EVERY n, VERIFIED ON MAIN (re-banks the SM seat's W109 proof, proof before checks before run, and its W108 census, rule before script before run; main re-derived the proof and ran an independent search; both seat scripts re-run): for every n >= 3 the only character of F_n in SL(2, C) fixed by every move R_ij (or every L_ij) is the trivial one -- one common trace t, Fricke forces t in {0, 2}, t = 0 makes the generators an orthonormal frame whose triple product has trace -/+2, t = 2 is trivial; at n = 2 the record's R and L fix exactly the trivial point and the quaternion point (0, 0, 0); on the class reading no finite subgroup of SU(2) has a fixed class for n >= 3 (a perfect image in a solvable Out(G)); W108: 2I at n = 3 has none, its 13 344 classes one orbit. So B1677 holds for every n with no SU(2) and no finite image assumed: two records follows from a non-trivial common character in SL(2, C), the finite image then forced (tr[a, b] = -2, Q8). The rank-two target stays priced. 0 of 19.
weave_or_thread: weave (every move of the weave of n records, every n)
